title: Interest rates, AI, and what comes next: Peter Linneman returns to the Walker Webcast
summary: Peter Linneman returns to the Walker Webcast to tackle interest rates, inflation, apartments, AI, and the U.S. economic outlook.
body_markdown:
Peter Linneman is returning to the[Walker Webcast](https://www.walkerdunlop.com/webcast) , and there will be no shortage of topics for him and[Willy Walker](https://www.walkerdunlop.com/about/people/willy-walker) to debate.


A longtime Walker Webcast favorite, Peter is known for combining economic data with candid analysis, memorable analogies, and a willingness to challenge conventional wisdom. With interest rates, inflation, geopolitical uncertainty, and shifting commercial real estate fundamentals all in focus, the timing of his return couldn’t be better.


Here’s a preview of what’s on the agenda.


## What’s really driving interest rates?


Interest rates are likely to be front and center.


But Peter is less interested in simply observing that rates have moved than in examining why they’ve moved and questioning some of the explanations being offered.


Expect Willy and Peter to explore the forces behind today’s rate environment, including inflation, energy prices, geopolitical uncertainty, and Federal Reserve policy. As longtime listeners already know, Peter has some characteristically strong opinions about the Fed.


The bigger question for commercial real estate is what today’s environment could mean for borrowing costs, investment decisions, and the economy in the months ahead.


## Is multifamily approaching a turning point?


The apartment market should provide another important topic for commercial real estate investors.


After a substantial wave of new supply, the development pipeline is changing. Peter believes that creates an important question: How long will it take individual apartment markets to regain their footing?


The answer won’t necessarily be the same everywhere. Some markets are already showing signs of improvement, even as they continue absorbing existing supply. Meanwhile, dramatically lower levels of new construction could change the equation in the years ahead.


Where—and when—could that create opportunities? Expect plenty to discuss.


## Debt, deficits, and the resilience of the U.S. economy


The national debt is another subject likely to generate a lively exchange.


Peter has previously challenged conventional fears about federal debt, and his latest thinking offers an unconventional framework for thinking about the issue.


It also connects to a much larger theme: the underlying resilience of the U.S. economy.


Peter has a new way of describing that resilience. It involves NBA star Victor Wembanyama and fictional action hero Jack Reacher.


Yes, really.


We’ll leave the explanation to Peter.


## What happens to jobs in the AI era?


Artificial intelligence could take the conversation in a completely different direction.


Rather than looking only at the jobs technology could eliminate, Peter considers the issue through the long arc of economic history: What happens when technology makes workers more productive, eliminates certain types of work, and creates entirely new categories of jobs?


It’s a debate with major implications for economic growth, employment, productivity, and ultimately commercial real estate.


Peter also has a prediction about AI’s very long-term future that is considerably less conventional. We won’t spoil it.


Interest rates. The Fed. Inflation. Apartments. Federal debt. Jobs. AI. And the future of the U.S. economy.


Peter’s return to the Walker Webcast promises to cover a lot of ground and, if past appearances are any indication, challenge a few assumptions along the way.


This is a must-see episode for anyone looking for answers in today’s CRE space. Be sure to[register for the episode here](https://events.zoom.us/ev/Ahc2L34K2p0zPCdgAbwqUITsQtlWt0BvChQr_mf6R1cpyAKqF41t~AocitLS8L54EoctDfl3G9dZ9koIwX7tVoJL4AK9VaC1HamRt5FedgWFg7WMN596ZGmsQ6suA2hYFuIUmAauCWKfysA) .
